title: What if sunlight switched off?
assumptions: Sun stops electromagnetic radiation but mass and gravity remain
No physically realistic mechanism implied; no exact cooling timeline

sources.supports: Sunlight travel time and solar energy
sources.access_status: not_verified_in_this_environment; NASA request received proxy 403 on 2026-10-25

scenes.label: AN IMPOSSIBLE SWITCH
scenes.text: What if sunlight switched off? Imagine the Sun stays in place, but suddenly stops emitting light.

scenes.label: LIGHT TAKES TIME
scenes.text: We would not notice immediately. Light already on its way would still travel toward Earth.

scenes.label: ABOUT EIGHT MINUTES
scenes.text: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us. Only after that delay would the sky change.

scenes.label: DARKNESS DOES NOT REMOVE MASS
scenes.text: In this scenario the Sun still has its mass. Darkness alone would not fling Earth out of its orbit.

scenes.label: COOLING TAKES TIME TOO
scenes.text: Earth would begin losing heat without its usual sunlight. Cooling and ecological effects would unfold over time.

scenes.label: DEFINE THE QUESTION
scenes.text: The lesson is to define the question. Turning off the light and removing the Sun are different experiments.
